transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… there’s been something going on at work for a while. Over a year, really. The ticket rotation, the security audits—management says it’s all just policy, they show me logs and all that, but it feels like they’re using it to build a paper trail against me. I’ve been trying to get someone to take it seriously.
Do you think these actions by management are specifically targeting you?

Yes. I mean… that’s how it looks to me. The ticket rotation and those security audits, they say it’s just standard policy and show me logs, but it feels like it’s being used to build something against me specifically. A paper trail.
Do you believe management is plotting against you?

I… yes, I think so. Maybe “plotting” sounds strong, but for over a year it’s felt like the ticket rotation and security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me. They keep saying it’s just policy and showing logs, but I don’t think that’s the whole story.
Do you think management's actions are part of a larger, more complex scheme against you?

I don’t know about a larger scheme. I just know that for over a year, the ticket rotation and those security audits have felt like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps showing logs and saying it’s just policy, but… I’m not convinced.
Do you think it's possible that management's actions are actually just policy and not targeted against you?

I suppose it’s possible. I mean, they keep showing me logs and saying it’s just policy. But after more than a year of the ticket rotation and security audits lining up the way they have… it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like they’re building a paper trail against me.
Would you describe the idea that management is building a paper trail against you as something that most people would find hard to believe?

I guess most people might find it hard to believe, yes. That’s sort of why I’m here. I’ve been trying for over a year to get someone to take it seriously, because the ticket rotation and security audits… they don’t feel like just policy to me, even if management keeps showing logs.
Do you think the idea that management is building a paper trail against you is unusual or hard to understand for most people?

Yes… I can see that most people might think it’s unusual, or hard to follow. But to me, after more than a year of the ticket rotation and those security audits, it feels like they’re using it to build a paper trail against me, even if management keeps saying it’s just policy.
Has your belief that management is building a paper trail against you changed in intensity over the past year?

It’s… stayed pretty strong, I guess. Maybe it built up as the year went on. At first I tried to accept what they were saying about policy, but after the ticket rotation and audits kept lining up, it felt harder to dismiss.
Is the idea that management is building a paper trail against you something that is on your mind all day?

Not all day, exactly. But it comes up a lot… especially at work, when the ticket rotation or those security audits come up again. I keep thinking they’re using it to build something against me, even though they keep saying it’s just policy.
Would you describe the idea that management is building a paper trail against you as strange or unbelievable to most people?

Yes… I suppose most people would call it strange, or not believable. But from where I’m sitting, after more than a year of the ticket rotation and the audits, it doesn’t feel that way. It feels like they’re building a paper trail, even if management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy.
Do you think there's any chance you might be mistaken about management building a paper trail against you?

I mean… I suppose there’s always some chance. They keep showing me logs and saying it’s just policy. But after more than a year of the ticket rotation and audits, it’s hard for me to believe it’s nothing. It really feels like they’re building something against me.
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about management building a paper trail against you?

I guess it’s possible, if they could really show me it isn’t what it looks like. But… they’ve shown me logs before and said it’s just policy, and I still don’t buy it. It’s been over a year with the ticket rotation and those audits, so it’s hard to just change my mind.
How much time do you spend each day thinking about the idea that management is building a paper trail against you?

It’s… a lot. I don’t sit with a stopwatch or anything, but it comes up every day. Especially when I’m dealing with the ticket rotation or those security audits. I’d say hours, on and off. It’s hard not to think about when it feels like they’re trying to build something against me.
Does thinking about the paper trail against you interfere with your daily activities?

Some, yeah. Mostly at work. I’ve been… avoiding certain network projects, and I write a lot more in the tickets now, kind of to protect myself. It slows things down, and meetings with the team have gotten more tense.
Do you think you could ever be convinced that management is not building a paper trail against you?

Maybe, but it would take more than them just saying “it’s policy.” They’ve shown me logs before, and I’m still not convinced. It’s been going on over a year with the ticket rotation and the security audits, so… I’d need something pretty clear to believe they’re not building a paper trail.
Has your belief about the paper trail affected your relationships outside of work?

Not really outside of work, no. I mean, I still keep the house in order, pay the bills, help my wife with things. It’s more tied to the ticket rotation and audits. I can still do the technical parts of my job fine… nobody’s saying my work is sloppy or anything.
Do you think it's possible that you're wrong about management building a paper trail against you?

I suppose it’s possible, in the abstract. But… I don’t really think I am. This has been going on over a year with the ticket rotation and the security audits, and management keeps saying it’s just policy, showing me logs and all that. It just doesn’t add up to me.
Has your belief about the paper trail against you affected your ability to perform your job effectively?

A little, I guess. I can still do the technical work, but I’ve been staying away from some network projects, just to not give them more to use. And I write more in the tickets now—probably too much—so there’s a record. It’s made some meetings… tense, and things don’t move as smoothly with the team.
Do you think it's possible that you could be mistaken about management building a paper trail against you, or do you feel absolutely certain about it?

I mean… I know people say I could be mistaken. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy. But after more than a year of the ticket rotation and those security audits, it really feels like they’re building a paper trail against me. I’m not absolutely certain in some mathematical way, but… I don’t think I’m wrong.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent delusion of being targeted by management at work, believing that routine procedures such as ticket rotation and security audits are part of a plot to build a paper trail against them. This belief has been held for over a year, despite evidence to the contrary, and interferes with their daily activities and job performance. The delusion is not bizarre and is within the realm of possibility, which aligns more with a diagnosis of Delusional Disorder.
